parameter: Medicaid check failure: adults subject to work rules who are employed
basis: Nebraska 2026: ~27% of subject adults and 15% of all adults checked lost coverage at renewal, 92% for paperwork; centered lower because most states will match data ex parte under CMS's June 2026 rule

parameter: Extra failure for subject adults not employed
basis: Cannot show 80 hours; some qualify through school or community service

parameter: Failure for exempt adults as a share of the subject rate
basis: Must still prove the exemption; Nebraska: 61% of those kept were exempt

parameter: Expansion adults exempt from work rules
basis: Parents of children 13 or younger, medically frail, students and others; Nebraska 2026

parameter: Employed share of subject adults
basis: Nebraska: 97% of compliant adults met the income test

parameter: Higher Medicaid failure for people already cut from SNAP
basis: Same paperwork and hours under both programs

parameter: Monthly re-enrollment after losing Medicaid
basis: Unwinding: about 1/3 re-enrolled within 90 days; under work rules a compliant month comes first

parameter: People losing Medicaid who find other coverage
basis: Arkansas 2018: no measurable rise in other coverage

parameter: Observed SNAP decline July 2025 to mid-2026
basis: USDA: 42.0M (July 2025) to 37.0M (April 2026); CBPP: more than 5M by June 2026

parameter: Share of that decline caused by the law
basis: Unemployment held near 4% while caseloads fell; some drop is other causes

parameter: Further SNAP losses during 2027
basis: State admin cost share from Oct 2026 and remaining waivers ending

parameter: Odds of a hospital stay after losing SNAP (participation)
basis: Samuel, Szanton et al. 2018: aOR 0.96 (0.93-0.99) for participating

parameter: Added odds per $10 of monthly benefit lost (study prices)
basis: Samuel, Szanton et al. 2018: aOR 0.99 per $10; benefit converted with food-at-home CPI (321.8 Sept 2026 vs ~226 in 2009-12)

parameter: ER visits after losing SNAP
basis: Same study found no significant ER effect

parameter: ER visits by the newly uninsured vs when insured
basis: Epic Research, 2023 unwinding: Medicaid share of ER visits -2.8 pts while self-pay rose 2.4 pts

parameter: Hospital stays by the newly uninsured vs when insured
basis: Epic Research 2026: self-pay inpatient share 1.9% to 2.6%; HCA: uninsured 10.5% of admissions vs 8.5% a year earlier

parameter: Unemployment rate Q4 2027
basis: Fed Sept 2026 median 4.1 (participants 4.0-4.5) widened for the Fed's own forecast errors and oil-shock risk after the 2026 Iran war (energy CPI +20.4%)

parameter: Monthly job loss among low-wage workers
basis: Scaled up or down with the unemployment rate

parameter: Monthly job finding
basis: Hiring weak: +29K payrolls in September 2026

parameter: Chance a hospital stay leads to job loss
basis: Dobkin et al.: hospital admission cuts employment 11 points over 3 years

parameter: Low-income Marketplace workers in non-expansion states who fall into the coverage gap after a job loss
basis: Yearly income drops below 100% of poverty; tax credit lost

parameter: 2026 Marketplace enrollment
basis: KFF: 19.2M effectuated Feb 2026; ~17.5M expected by year end

parameter: Uncompensated care passed on to commercial premiums
basis: Studies find limited cost shifting; hospitals absorb most through margins and DSH and local funds

parameter: Links between inputs
basis: Shared administrative-friction factor (Medicaid; SNAP; Marketplace) and economy factor (unemployment; job loss; job finding)
